profile_revisions.what: The נוהל text is unchanged. (1) spec.json gains `spatial_coverage_wording`: Spatial coverage is written as the נוהל asks (ארצי / מטרופולין / יישוב) or by the official administrative name (מחוז, אזור יהודה ושומרון) and never as 'the occupied territories' in any language - build writes TODO and records the refusal in _meta.refused_wording, validate reports spatial_coverage_wording (error) at the dataset and file level; a profile may add a term, never remove one. (2) Size / File size carry the fitting unit AND the exact byte count (e.g. '16.5 MB (17,268,557 bytes)') instead of a rounded MB number that turned small files into 0.0. (3) Parquet tables are scanned (pyarrow: schema types, exact row count, samples) and aligned with the metadata like any CSV, on disk and inside a zip.

profile_revisions.source: owner rule 2026-08-26, on-board viewer project (docs/KIT-PROPOSALS.md KP-28)
profile_revisions.what: The נוהל text is unchanged. spec.json gains `unknown_tokens`: a required TEXT key answered with an explicit documented-unknown token is answered (info value_unknown_documented, printed as such in the report), while an empty cell, TODO, and the listed placeholders (?, N/A, -, ...) remain errors. Keys with a shape (date/e-mail/URL) or a closed vocabulary are out of scope - 'unknown' is not an answer to those. A profile may add a token, never remove one.

profile_revisions.source: owner rule 2026-08-26, on-board viewer project (docs/KIT-PROPOSALS.md KP-27, KP-28, KP-30, KP-31)
profile_revisions.what: The FORMAT text is unchanged. (1) KP-27: the codes Table 11 defines for zone_id_orig/zone_id_dest (-1 abroad, -2 Palestinian localities, -3 IDF/IPS camps, -4 unknown) index nothing in zones.zip by design, so they are excluded from join_orphans and zone_code_unresolved - numerator and denominator - and reported as an info zone_special_codes with per-code row counts; the codes are read from the profile's own `Values`, never hard-coded. (2) KP-31: zones.zip carries key_role=lookup, so it is the parent of its join whichever side of the arrow the format writes it on; the orphans are the codes the layer does not index, not the zones nobody travelled to. (3) KP-28: a required text key (Contractor rows, Author, Contact) may carry an explicit unknown token - see the base dictionary's unknown_tokens; an empty cell, ?, TODO and N/A stay errors. (4) KP-30: a .dbf that declares no encoding is decoded with the .cpg, then UTF-8, then its own code page byte, then Windows-1255, reported as dbf_encoding_assumed - a layer read under a named assumption beats a layer with no documented fields at all.

profile_revisions.source: proposals from the on-board viewer project, 2026-08 (docs/KIT-PROPOSALS.md, KP-1..KP-26), raised while driving the kit over 18 real on-board deliveries
profile_revisions.what: The FORMAT text is unchanged. What changed is the profile's reading of it: delivery zips exempt from field documentation (Table 5), a counts-only package does not owe obod.csv/zones.zip (two conditions), expected documents (report/methodology at warning, questionnaire at info), zones-layer key candidates + --deep zones, CBS statistical-areas field descriptions shipped (references/cbs-fields.json), expected_keys may be alternatives (trip_index | trip_id), not_recorded as an accepted token, month_year m_yyyy/mm_yyyy/m_m_yyyy, Data encoding per file, Contractor roles, Zones type spelling normalised, orig/dest_lat_lon required* + distribution:false.
deferred_to_the_format_author: Sample size passengers: rows in obod.csv or passengers counted in obad.csv (FP-18)
trips -> obad/obod key: 3.8 prints trip_id, 3.6 and Tables 10-11 name trip_index (FP-14) - the kit accepts both
a per-file synonym table for real-world column names (KP-1) - vocabulary, not typography

profile_revisions.source: בקשת הבעלים, 06/09/2026: "שיוודא שאין בעייה של כתיבת סימני שאלה במקום מלל בעברית" (KP-R3, rail-viewer/docs/KIT-PROPOSALS.md)
profile_revisions.what: The נוהל text is unchanged. spec.json gains `encoding_integrity`: Hebrew is never written as question marks, checked at the three points where it silently happens. (1) Data files: a text column whose values are a run of `?` (or where `?` is at least half the characters), or which holds U+FFFD, is reported once per column as text_lost_as_question_marks (error) with the count and up to three examples; a column whose Hebrew is Windows-1252 mojibake - UTF-8 read as cp1252 (the lead pairs the dictionary lists) or cp1255 read as cp1252 (a run of accented Latin letters) - is hebrew_mojibake (error). The counts come from the sample the scanner already profiles, so the check costs nothing extra, and it counts values, never judges their content. (2) The metadata document's own strings - header, blocks, file descriptions, field descriptions, labels - get the same test as metadata_value_question_marks (error); a lone `?` stays a value_placeholder, as before. (3) The kit's own outputs: every json/xlsx/csv/html it writes is read back and each Hebrew string of the document must return character for character (output_roundtrip_failed, error, build exits 2 - this is the kit's own bug, never the user's), and a PDF's first two pages must yield the title's Hebrew to pypdf (pdf_hebrew_not_rendered, warning, build exits non-zero unless --allow-unverified-pdf; without pypdf the check is skipped with an info, never assumed to pass). The console fallback stays and a line that had to be degraded is prefixed '[console: degraded encoding] '. Thresholds, mojibake markers and wording are data; a profile may tighten a threshold or add a marker, never remove one, and the severities belong to the base dictionary alone.

The נוהל text and the profile texts are unchanged. A token a FORMAT accepts as a cell value (`accepted_tokens` - `Null`, `not_recorded`) is a category of its own, so no check that classifies cell values may read it as data. `Spec.accepted_tokens` / `accepted_token_set` / `is_accepted_token` expose the merged list (base + profile; the base נוהל names none, a profile may add and never remove), and `type_implausible` now ignores an accepted token exactly as `value_undocumented` already did - a numeric column that holds the format's token beside its codes is not mistyped. The scanner reports which values are not numeric (`non_numeric_values`, value -> row count, up to 20 distinct) so the judgement is exact: real free text beside a token is still a warning, with the tokens left out of the count and the examples. A column with no value at all no longer contradicts its declared type. With no profile nothing is ignored.
